title: Set F-Droid to check for updates weekly and install them in the background
instruction: In the F-Droid app, configure the settings to automatically check for updates on a weekly basis and enable the background automatic installation of updates.

steps.thought: the user needs me to get into the F-Droid settings. My first and most obvious step is to actually launch the F-Droid application itself. I'm looking for it on my home screen, but it doesn't seem to be there. No worries, that's a common scenario. I'll simply swipe up from the bottom of the screen to access the app drawer, where I can then locate and open F-Droid.

The app drawer is open. I need to find F-Droid.
The apps are sorted alphabetically. I see apps starting with A, B, C, D. F-Droid should be further down.
I will swipe up to scroll down the app drawer.

I scrolled too far. I see apps starting with M, N, O, P, R, S, T, W, Y.
I need to scroll back up to find F-Droid.

Ah, I swiped down too much and ended up back on the home screen.
Let's open the app drawer again.

I'm back in the app drawer. I see apps starting with A, B, C, D.
I need to scroll down a bit to find F-Droid. I'll do a smaller swipe this time.

Great, I see F-Droid now. It's in the second row, on the far right.
I will click on the F-Droid icon to open it.

F-Droid is open. The user wants me to configure settings.
I see a "Settings" tab at the bottom right corner.
I will click on the "Settings" tab.
From left to right, they probably represent: Never, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Every 2 weeks, Monthly, etc. Wait, let's look at the slider. It has 7 dots.

If moving right decreases the interval, then moving left should increase it.
Let's try clicking the 3rd dot (one to the left of the middle).
The 3rd dot is around x=360, y=810.
Both requirements are met. I can terminate the task successfully.
